sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Inter-Annotator Agreement Studio. In this lab, you can directly edit the two-by-two contingency matrix between two independent raters. Notice how raw agreement P_o, expected chance P_e, and Cohen's Kappa update in real time. Click the High Prevalence Paradox preset to observe 96 percent raw agreement collapse to a failing Kappa of 0.323.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Try the High Prevalence Paradox button, Dr. Nova! Even with 96 percent raw agreement, Cohen's Kappa plunges into the red zone because chance agreement was 94.1 percent!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: Two radiologists review 10,000 screening mammograms with 0.5 percent malignancy prevalence. They agree on 9,900 Negative and 20 Positive scans, disagreeing on 80 scans, giving 99.2 percent raw agreement. What is their Cohen's Kappa, and what is the engineering verdict?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, let's see if our engineers can spot what happens to Cohen's Kappa when 99.2 percent raw agreement is evaluated against high-prevalence chance marginals!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on, Quality Architect! Marginal probabilities yield expected chance agreement P_e of 98.81 percent. Cohen's Kappa is only 0.329, falling into the Poor Reliability tier. The radiologists disagreed on 80 percent of actual positive detection opportunities!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Do not be deceived by 99.2 percent raw agreement. In high-prevalence asymmetry, chance agreement P_e is 98.81 percent. Cohen's Kappa evaluates the remaining window and equals only 0.329, signaling unacceptable reliability.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In the Dawid-Skene Consensus Studio, observe the four clinical items voted on by three workers. On Item 2, Worker 1 votes Class 1, but noisy Worker 2 and spammer Worker 3 vote Class 0. Click Step EM Algorithm to watch the posterior update and flip Item 2 to Class 1 with over 91 percent confidence.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at Item 2, Dr. Nova! Naive majority voting picked Class 0 two-to-one, but Dawid-Skene recognized Worker 1's 98 percent accuracy and correctly recovered Class 1!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: In content safety moderation, 5 annotators label comments. Worker 1 is a verified specialist with 98 percent accuracy and 1 percent false positive rate. Workers 2 through 5 are click-farm bots always submitting zero. On an overtly toxic comment, Worker 1 votes 1 while Workers 2 through 5 vote 0. What are the outcomes under Majority Voting versus Dawid-Skene EM?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Four click-farm bots vote 0 against one senior specialist who votes 1! Does democracy win, or does Dawid-Skene save the dataset?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely right! Majority voting fails 4-to-1, allowing hate speech into the training set. Dawid-Skene recognizes Worker 1's near-zero false positive rate, making the Class 0 likelihood contain a 0.01 multiplier and resolving True Class 1 with over 95 percent confidence!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Remember that naive majority voting gives equal weight to all five votes, wrongly adopting the 4-to-1 bot consensus. Dawid-Skene uses the learned confusion matrices to heavily discount the bots and trust Worker 1.
